_comment: Every command below sources ONE interpreter probe, `hooks/probe-python.sh`,
then checks the POSTCONDITION it actually needs: `$PYEXE` is set. That
script carries the full rationale — why it RUNS each candidate instead of
trusting `command -v`, why the version comes back on stdout as one byte, why
the three names are not sufficient, and why refusal is non-zero but
fail-open. Read it before changing anything here.
The probe used to be a 350-char one-liner inlined into all five commands,
plus a `_pyexe` reference copy in this file. JSON has no substitution, so
the copies were held equal only by a test, and they had drifted from the
reference once already. Both the duplication and `_pyexe` are gone; the
script is the single source, and `test_every_wiring_sources_the_shared_probe`
pins that every command still reaches it.
WHY THE CHECK IS `-x` AND NOT `-n`. Measured, on a truncated CRLF probe
under dash: the probe's first statement is the ASSIGNMENT `PYEXE=`, so a
trailing CR makes it `PYEXE=<CR>` — set, non-empty, and useless. `-n` passed
it and the wiring ran `<CR> some-hook.py`; `-x` refuses it. `[ -x "" ]` is
false too, so `-x` subsumes the emptiness check rather than adding to it.
WHY THE CHECK IS A POSTCONDITION AND NOT `. probe || { ... }`. The first
form of this wiring chained the failure clause to `.`, which misses the case
extraction created: a probe file that is PRESENT but empty or truncated. `.`
returns 0 on a zero-byte file, so the clause never fired and the wiring ran
`"" some-hook.py` — measured rc=127 on bash, sh AND dash, tool call
proceeds, output `: command not found`, naming neither cla nor the probe.
A truncated hooks.json was invalid JSON and loaded nothing; a truncated .sh
degrades to silence. `[ -r "$_cla_probe" ]` also keeps `.` from FAILING,
which matters because sh and dash abort on a failed `.` and never reach a
trailing clause — so on the shells Claude Code documents for macOS/Linux the
plugin's own diagnostic was never printed. Verified: identical message and
rc=1 on bash, sh and dash, for a missing probe and a zero-byte one.
`PYEXE=;` leads every command for the same reason it leads the probe. The
probe clears it, but the probe only runs when the file is readable — so
without this clear, a missing probe plus an exported `PYEXE` would satisfy
the postcondition and hand every hook a stale interpreter.

hooks.command: PYEXE=; _cla_probe="${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/probe-python.sh"; [ -r "$_cla_probe" ] && . "$_cla_probe"; [ -x "$PYEXE" ] || { echo "cla: interpreter probe at $_cla_probe is missing or unusable — guard hooks are NOT running" >&2; exit 1; }; "$PYEXE" "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/dispatch-edit-write-pretooluse.py"
